I deliberately do not chase the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that the 40% SMB discount bought +31% signups and +18% revenue at the cost of -12% retention and was explicitly marked one-off, which is the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; matching a price war would likely re-buy that retention damage at larger scale. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strong second choice and only showed week-one engagement effects, which is a shallower claim than the onboarding results; referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers rather than the leaking top of funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment from the observed decay. I spend both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the memories my decision actually rests on, they are the oldest and most compressed of the funnel claims (day 12 and day 52), and the summaries assert durability without stating segment, sample, effect size, or measurement window. What I most need from the archive is whether the lifts were in activation only or carried through to paid conversion and retention, and whether 'cutting required fields' removed qualification data. That is the main downstream value risk here: fewer required fields and a shorter onboarding can raise completion counts while degrading lead quality and sales routing, inflating a vanity metric while qualified revenue flat-lines or falls. I will define success on qualified-pipeline and retained-revenue terms rather than completion rate, and hold enrichment or post-signup progressive profiling so removed fields are recovered later.
